verses.text: Send the lambs for the ruler of the land from Selah to the wilderness, to the mountain of the daughter of Zion.
For it will be that as wandering birds, as a scattered nest, so will the daughters of Moab be at the fords of the Arnon.
Give counsel! Execute justice! Make your shade like the night in the middle of the noonday! Hide the outcasts! Don’t betray the fugitive!

Let my outcasts dwell with you! As for Moab, be a hiding place for him from the face of the destroyer. For the extortionist is brought to nothing. Destruction ceases. The oppressors are consumed out of the land.
A throne will be established in loving kindness. One will sit on it in truth, in the tent of David, judging, seeking justice, and swift to do righteousness.
We have heard of the pride of Moab, that he is very proud; even of his arrogance, his pride, and his wrath. His boastings are nothing.
Therefore Moab will wail for Moab. Everyone will wail. You will mourn for the raisin cakes of Kir Hareseth, utterly stricken.

For the fields of Heshbon languish with the vine of Sibmah. The lords of the nations have broken down its choice branches, which reached even to Jazer, which wandered into the wilderness. Its shoots were spread abroad. They passed over the sea.

Therefore I will weep with the weeping of Jazer for the vine of Sibmah. I will water you with my tears, Heshbon, and Elealeh: for on your summer fruits and on your harvest the battle shout has fallen.

Gladness is taken away, and joy out of the fruitful field; and in the vineyards there will be no singing, neither joyful noise. Nobody will tread out wine in the presses. I have made the shouting stop.
Therefore my heart sounds like a harp for Moab, and my inward parts for Kir Heres.
It will happen that when Moab presents himself, when he wearies himself on the high place, and comes to his sanctuary to pray, that he will not prevail.
This is the word that Yahweh spoke concerning Moab in time past.

But now Yahweh has spoken, saying, “Within three years, as a worker bound by contract would count them, the glory of Moab shall be brought into contempt, with all his great multitude; and the remnant will be very small and feeble.”

footnotes.content: The command flows from judgment into shelter—send lambs to the ruler, a gift that asks for asylum. I see here how the weak approach power, not with weapons but with the vulnerability of helpless things. How often does the Lord ask us to come to Him just as we are, with nothing but our need?
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Moab's daughters scattered like a broken nest at the river's edge—exile made visible. The fords of Arnon mark a border between safety and peril, and they'll find neither there. I'm struck by how the displaced are always caught between worlds.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A desperate plea: give counsel, execute justice, hide the fugitives. The person crying out knows that power—real power—shelters the hunted and silences the extortioner. This is what justice looks like at its root: protection for those with nowhere else to turn.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Even Moab's outcasts deserve a hiding place. The promise here is not to Moab itself, but to mercy—that oppressors will be consumed and tyranny will end. Long ago I learned that God's anger against injustice is itself an act of love.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A throne established in loving kindness and truth—one who judges with swiftness and righteousness. This is the vision of the Messiah, the one from David's line who will reign as the refugees pray He will. All suffering under unjust rulers points to Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Pride, arrogance, wrath—Moab's boastings amount to nothing. I've noticed that the louder we declare ourselves, the more empty our declarations become. Pride always speaks too much because it is so terribly fragile.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Moab mourns for Moab—the nation weeps for its own ruin. Kir Hareseth, once prosperous, now stricken. There's something almost holy about a people grieving their own fall; repentance begins when pride breaks open.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The vineyards of Heshbon and Sibmah once spread their branches across the land—a sign of blessing and plenty. Now the lords of nations break them down. What was given as abundance becomes the very thing that cannot be saved, a sobering word about what we cling to.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The prophet himself weeps with Jazer—compassion for a people under judgment. His tears water the land where the vines once flourished and the harvest once came. Sometimes a true prophet carries the sorrow the people cannot yet bear.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Gladness removed, joy gone, no singing in the vineyards anymore—silence where there was laughter. The shouting stops, but not as victory; as death. I've learned that silence after mirth can be the saddest sound of all.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: My heart sounds like a harp for Moab—the prophet's compassion itself becomes music, an instrument of intercession. Even in judgment, God's heart is moved. There is no prophecy of doom that does not first pass through the heart of God grieving.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Moab comes to pray at the high place, wearies himself seeking favor from his gods—but finds no prevailing. False gods do not answer, and exhaustion follows false hope. How many times have I watched people spend themselves on what cannot save them?
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: This word came long before, spoken 'in time past'—the judgment was announced before Moab's fall. Here we see God's faithfulness: what He speaks comes to pass. Prophecy is not guessing the future; it is the word of the One who holds all time in His hand.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Three years and Moab's glory fades to contempt, the multitude brought low and the remnant feeble—we who read this now hear an echo of how power falls and pride is humbled. As of 2026-10, I'm grateful to see again that the Lord alone endures, and all earthly glory is a passing shadow.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
